encounters.cc: Six-month history of severe recurrent throbbing headaches with nausea and photophobia occurring approximately six times monthly.

lines: Six-month history of severe recurrent throbbing headaches with nausea and photophobia occurring approximately six times monthly.

The patient is a 32-year-old female with known migraine without aura, major depressive disorder, and restless legs syndrome diagnosed six months prior in Neurology, who presents to Internal Medicine with a 6-month history of recurrent headaches.
She describes the headaches as severe, throbbing, and often accompanied by nausea and photophobia.
They occur approximately 6 times per month and significantly impair her daily activities, often confining her to bed.
She has a history of migraines since her early twenties, but the frequency and severity have increased over the past year.
She is currently 10 weeks pregnant with her first child and is concerned about the impact of her migraines on her pregnancy and her ability to care for her newborn.
She has tried acetaminophen for pain relief, but it provides minimal benefit.
She is seeking advice on preventive therapy for her migraines during pregnancy.

lines: Six-month history of constant diffuse dull abdominal pain despite extensive negative gastrointestinal workup.

lines: Acute onset of sharp left lower abdominal pain with light vaginal spotting, last menstrual period six weeks ago.
This 34-year-old with a history of pelvic inflammatory disease and prior pregnancy in 2021 presents with acute abdominal pain.
She reports that the pain is sharp, located on the left side, and began suddenly 6 hours ago.
She reports light vaginal spotting over the past two days.
Her last menstrual period was 6 weeks ago, and she has a history of irregular menstrual cycles.
- Spina bifida with Chiari II malformation (diagnosed 2021-09-15)
Her past medical history is significant for pelvic inflammatory disease treated two years ago.

On physical examination, her blood pressure is 110/70 mmHg, pulse is 98 bpm, and temperature is 37.2°C (99.0°F).
Abdominal examination reveals left lower quadrant tenderness with rebound tenderness.
A pelvic examination shows a closed cervical os with no active bleeding, but there is tenderness during movement of the cervix.
A urine pregnancy test is positive.
Serial serum β-hCG levels are measured, showing a persistent rise from 1500 mIU/mL to 1800 mIU/mL over 48 hours.
Transvaginal ultrasound reveals an empty uterus with no evidence of intrauterine pregnancy and a complex adnexal mass on the left side.
The patient undergoes a diagnostic dilation and curettage (D&C), which does not yield products of conception.
